title: Microsoft Entra ID Overview
description: Learn what Microsoft Entra ID is, how it protects identities, and why every Azure application needs it.

data.text: Microsoft Entra ID is Azure's cloud-based identity and access management service. Think of it as the security guard for your applications and users in the cloud. It stores user accounts, checks passwords, and decides who can access what.
Every Azure developer works with Entra ID because almost every Azure service uses it to authenticate users and services. Understanding Entra ID is the foundation for securing any cloud application.

data.title: What Entra ID Manages
items: Applications that need to sign in

terms.definition: A digital representation of a person, service, or device.
A dedicated instance of Entra ID for your organization.
Verifying who someone or something is.
Deciding what an authenticated identity is allowed to do.

data.text: How Entra ID fits into a request

When an application needs to call an Azure service, it does not send a password. It asks Entra ID for a token from the tenant authority endpoint, `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant-id}`. Entra ID verifies the caller (a user session, a client secret, a certificate, a managed identity assertion, or a federated OIDC token) and returns a signed JWT. The target service then validates the token signature, issuer, audience, and expiry before allowing the call.

Because the token is the proof, the important questions become: which tenant issued it, which application or user is it for (the audience), which scopes were consented, and how long is it valid. Almost every Azure security incident involving identity comes back to one of those four properties being too broad.

data.title: Inspect your signed-in context
data.content: The Azure CLI is already authenticated through Entra ID, so you can inspect the tenant, user, and subscription it is using.
data.code:
az account show --query "{tenant:tenantId, user:user.name, subscription:name}" -o json
az ad signed-in-user show --query "{id:id, upn:userPrincipalName}" -o table

data.text: Entra ID is not on-premises Active Directory

Developers often assume Entra ID is "Active Directory in the cloud". It is not. Entra ID is a flat directory with no organizational units, no Group Policy, and no LDAP. It speaks modern protocols: OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, and SAML. Organizations that need both worlds run Entra Connect to synchronize on-premises accounts into the tenant, but authentication and authorization decisions in Azure are made by Entra ID.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: Be precise about the two boundaries. A tenant is the identity boundary: it owns users, groups, and app registrations. A subscription is a billing and management boundary that trusts exactly one tenant. "One tenant can own many subscriptions, and a subscription cannot span tenants" is the sentence that shows you understand the model.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Entra ID is Azure's identity platform — it manages users, apps, and access policies.
A tenant is your organization's dedicated Entra ID instance.
Authentication proves identity; authorization grants permissions.
data.takeaway: If your app runs in Azure, it will interact with Entra ID. Start here.
